name: Rheology
boundaries: Rheology: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: A universal constitutive equation for all complex fluids
original_dispositions.reason: Covered primarily by RHE-01, with the class-specific principles left in RHE-02, RHE-03, RHE-05, and RHE-11. A single extra ID would have erased those distinctions. The claim that Journal of Rheology volume 70, number 1 is an official special issue listing the ten items is false; the issue contains ordinary papers plus the ring-polymer perspective.

original_dispositions.original_title: A complete theory of shear banding and elastic instabilities, plus a universal way to suppress them
original_dispositions.reason: Covered in part by RHE-08 for elastic and elasto-inertial turbulence, and by RHE-01 for the requirement that a closure predict banding when the flow type changes. Not added as its own concept. Steady shear banding of wormlike micelles already has a mechanistic account from a non-monotonic constitutive curve. Quantitative prediction for real formulations, edge fracture, and rheo-chaos remain open and important. A universal suppressor for every processing instability would be an application of RHE-01 and RHE-08.

original_dispositions.original_title: A multiscale theory of ring and branched polymer rheology
original_dispositions.reason: Split because the topologies differ. Branched melts with free ends are covered by RHE-04. Rings are added as RHE-11.

This is a methods problem. Pieces already exist, including velocity profiling and partitioned fixtures. Making every measurement cleaner does not, by itself, create a constitutive principle or a previously impossible flow. RHE-07 is the closest retained capability, changing the observable from wall torque to local stress.

original_dispositions.original_title: Nonlocal rheology for inhomogeneous and confined flows
A thermodynamic theory of active rheology
A general theory of thixotropy, aging, and rheological memory
original_dispositions.reason: History-dependent structure is part of what RHE-01 has to carry. New structural-kinetics models continue to appear, including a partially reversible model in Physics of Fluids 38, 106804, DOI 10.1063/5.0348133; this is model-building on a known idea. The historical claim about 4D-printed programmable matter adds a manufacturing step the rheological law would not by itself deliver. Field-addressable latching is a different capability, already RHE-06.

original_dispositions.original_title: A master theory of extensional rheology and strain hardening
original_dispositions.reason: Covered by RHE-01 for transfer from shear to extension in a general fluid, and by RHE-04 for branched-melt hardening. Filament-thinning methods are improving; a better extensional fixture is not a separate revolution.

original_dispositions.original_title: A granular law with shape, friction, and polydispersity
original_dispositions.reason: Covered by RHE-03. Kamrin and coauthors already treat shape and polydispersity as the agenda beyond μ(I), and that agenda is unfinished.

original_dispositions.original_title: A quantum-to-continuum link for nanoscale confined rheology
original_dispositions.reason: No inspected source supports a quantum constitutive principle as the missing rheological discovery. Gap-dependent viscosity, slip, and layering in nanogaps are real boundary-condition problems. The historical consequences need further device and surface-chemistry breakthroughs that were not evidenced here. Calling the gap “quantum” overstates it.

reconciliation_change_log.change: RHE-01 through RHE-10 kept their IDs and their subjects. No first-pass concept was deleted or merged away.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The first-pass concepts are all retained under the same IDs.

reconciliation_change_log.change: RHE-01 now says explicitly that a single all-fluids equation is this kinematic problem plus the other principles, and it records the British Society sentences on wormlike-micelle equations of state and on frame-invariant learning.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Preserve the distinction between kinematic transfer and class-specific principles.

reconciliation_change_log.change: RHE-03 names Kamrin, Hill, Goldman, and Andrade, quotes their scope limit on μ(I), and adds the British Society sentence on friction and adhesion.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Record the scope of existing granular models and the remaining difficulty with non-ideal materials.

reconciliation_change_log.change: RHE-04 is fenced off from rings.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Ring polymers have a different topology from branched melts.

reconciliation_change_log.change: RHE-05 records the active-colloid review as a title only.
RHE-08 absorbs the 2026 periodic-box “ultimate state” of elastic turbulence and the March 2026 entangled-polymer simulation, and cites the 1993 banding mechanism.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The 1993 mechanism should not be treated as missing; the 2026 results are partial advances.

reconciliation_change_log.change: RHE-10 drops an unverified DOI for the Mader review and keeps the publisher URL.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The DOI was not re-verified digit by digit.

reconciliation_change_log.change: RHE-11 is new: ring topology is a missing constitutive principle, with a disputed viscosity exponent and a chromosome motivation that is not yet a demonstrated identity.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The ring-polymer case has a different topology from branched melts.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Historical items 4, 7, and 10 were not given IDs.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The reasons are recorded in their historical dispositions.
